title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that compared an LLM‑only suggestion pipeline to a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task selection rule (K=200 tasks), a single shared generator output per task, and a deterministic validator, we observed: baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded (verify→repair) validator passes = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. No repair call was invoked (0 repairs across 200 guarded episodes). Under the tested model (requested_model=gpt-5-mini) and the preregistered sampling/validator contract, H1 is not supported: we detect no marginal verifier benefit. All execution, scoring, and validator traces are archived (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6) for replay and audit.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation is attractive for NetOps, but erroneous changes can cause reachability regressions and service disruption. Architectures that pair a generative model with a deterministic verifier and an optional repair step (generate→verify→repair, G→V→R) are widely proposed to reduce such operational risk. However, causal estimates of the verifier’s marginal effect under preregistered, artifact‑archived conditions are scarce. We therefore preregistered and ran a paired experiment (cand-002-gvr-loop) that isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect by: (i) deterministically selecting tasks from a public synthetic pool using SHA‑256(intent) sorting; (ii) using a single shared generator output per task that both arms evaluate (shared_initial_generation); and (iii) allowing at most one repair call in the guarded arm. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (binary validator pass rate difference within task).
sections.related_work: Recent work highlights generate–validate–repair pipelines and verifier‑augmented agentic NetOps prototypes (e.g., Cornetto and related generate–validate–repair literature). Parallel proposals emphasize confining LLMs to translation and relying on solvers for provable reasoning. Benchmarks and surveys document the promise and failure modes of LLMs in NetOps; our study complements these by providing a preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired causal estimate under a deterministic sampling and validation contract. All cited background works used for positioning were verified and appear in the evidence bundle (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental contract. The study preregistration (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622) froze task selection, inclusion rules, metrics, stopping rules, and the statistical analysis before observing outcomes. Task selection: tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and included only if the preregistered deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) covered the required features. Selection applied a deterministic SHA‑256(intent_string) sort and took the first K=200 unique tasks; the manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7621f83208298f5c8d965bcdbba115e741f95a1efb92944347b35bbf0). Model and adapter. The requested model identifier was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa) running under adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1.
sections.results: Execution summary and primary outcome (artifact‑grounded). Planned episodes = 400 (two arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes = 400. Model calls used = 200 (one shared generator call per task; no repair calls invoked). Primary paired counts: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). Baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded validator passes = 200/200. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 52a0858d682f588d7072b5f8a3b13fa62ab84ffda98a3aaee96151dfbf450e20). Repair invocation accounting. The repair pathway was never required: repair_applied = false for all 200 guarded episodes; model_calls_used=200 confirms no extra repair model calls were performed (execution/execution_manifest.json). Representative scoring JSONs and validator traces are archived under execution/scoring/ (examples: task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874cebd979af0ded1859e51e6f51d937b5f9967d62c73f439aa52a257cc).
sections.discussion: Statistical interpretation of the degenerate outcome. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate (~0.20). Observing baseline = 0.0 across 200 tasks places the run in a ceiling regime: with zero discordant pairs the exact McNemar test yields p = 1.00 and the bootstrap percentile CI collapses to the point [0.00,0.00]; this is the mathematically correct descriptive inference for the sampled regime. It does not prove the verifier is useless in general; it shows that under the tested model, deterministic sampling rule, and validator coverage the generator outputs already satisfied the validator constraints. Why repairs were not invoked. Three artifact‑grounded, non‑overlapping factors explain the null outcome: (1) inclusion required validator coverage, biasing the pool toward cases the validator can assess; (2) the chosen generator (gpt-5-mini) produced candidates that matched task workflow constraints (per‑task normalized_configuration equals the reference in execution/scoring/*.json); (3) the shared_initial_generation design fixes the generator output across arms and therefore prevents regeneration that might have produced validator‑failing candidates. These provenance facts are archived (execution/model_configuration.json, execution/responses/, execution/scoring/).
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered paired contract and the tested model (gpt-5-mini), we observed no verifier marginal benefit: baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00, McNemar p = 1.00, bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair path was never invoked (0 repairs across 200 guarded episodes). This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6). We emphasize scope limits: the outcome does not generalize to failure‑rich production distributions or other models; we recommend future confirmatory designs intentionally sample or construct failure‑rich tasks, evaluate multiple generator strengths, and consider interactive generator–verifier estimands if the research question is closed‑loop improvement. The archived artifacts and manifest enable exact replay and independent auditing.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model=gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Deterministic synthetic task pool and the preregistered inclusion rule (validator coverage required) bias the sample toward cases the validator supports and limit external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would mask regressions that matter in production.

Design constraint: shared_initial_generation fixes the generator output across arms and prevents adaptive regeneration; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates, not closed‑loop generator–verifier improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) rendered the preregistered power calculation (targeting baseline ≈ 0.20) inapplicable; inference is descriptive and artifact‑grounded for the tested regime.
